plain: Payment or repayment for a service, loss or harm

webster.text: To compensate; to make return of an equivalent for any thing given, done or suffered; as, to recompense a person for services, for fidelity or for sacrifices of time, for loss or damages.

more.text: To make an equivalent return in profit or produce.

example.quote: The excises were designed as a recompense to the importing states for relinquishing their imposts.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, June 28, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
